newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA BUILD HANDY LEAD AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BUILD HANDY LEAD AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: India took the upper hand by stretching their overall lead to 228 runs against South Africa at tea on the third day of the third and final test on Tuesday.
India, with a 60-run first innings lead, were 168 for four in their second innings with skipper Sachin Tendulkar on 31 and Mohammed Azharuddin on 26.
Night watchman Anil Kumble (42) and left-hander Saurav Ganguly (41) were the only two wickets to fall after lunch in a session which yielded 89 runs.

Kumble, who came in at the fall of opener Woorkeri Raman's wicket on Monday evening, struck five boundaries in his 144-minute knock before he was caught by Herschelle Gibbs at point off pace bowler Fanie de Villiers.
De Villiers was the most successful South African bowler so far, picking up two wickets for 39 runs.
Ganguly, who hit six boundaries in his 41 runs, was caught by Brian McMillan at silly-point off spinner Pat Symcox.
Ganguly's dismissal at 121 brought together Tendulkar and Azharuddin.
Tendulkar has hit five boundaries while Azharuddin has despatched the ball to the fence four times.
Opener Nayan Mongia departed in the 10th over of the day when pace bowler Lance Klusener trapped him leg before wicket for 18.
